items.title: 13.10.1 Reaction with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide

source_refs.note: Topic 13.10.1 with the Keep in Mind box, printed page 300.

blocks.text: Chlorine disproportionates with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide, forming sodium chloride and sodium chlorate(I), NaClO (formerly called sodium hypochlorite): Cl2(g) + 2NaOH(aq) gives NaCl(aq) + NaClO(aq) + H2O(l). The oxidation states of chlorine are 0 in Cl2, -1 in NaCl and +1 in NaClO: chlorine is oxidised from 0 to +1 in NaClO and reduced from 0 to 1 in NaCl, the simultaneous oxidation and reduction that makes this a disproportionation.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says chlorine is reduced from 0 to 1 in NaCl; the minus sign is missing. Chlorine in NaCl is -1, so it is reduced from 0 to -1.
Show that the reaction of Cl2 with cold aqueous KOH is a disproportionation.
